title: Autonomous Reward Engineering with Google ADK
subtitle: Hands-On Implementation: Build a Eureka-like reward learning pipeline with Google ADK, Brax physics, and parallel GPU evaluation.

lessons.title: Agent Design, Code Structure & ADK Workflow
lessons.hook: NVIDIA's original Eureka system runs on enterprise GPU clusters with proprietary physics simulators. How can we re-engineer and orchestrate this closed-loop reward evolution pipeline as a lightweight, modular agent architecture using Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) and Brax physics?
lessons.bigIdea: By decomposing Eureka into distinct cooperating agents orchestrated via Google ADK, we implement a practical reward evolution pipeline: a Sequential entry point separates one-time environment initialization (SetupAgent) from an iterative agentic loop (RewardEvolutionLoop). Inside the loop, specialized agents handle generation (RewardDesigner), execution (CandidateEvaluator), comparison (Selector), diagnosis (RewardReflector), and termination control (ExitChecker).
lessons.plainEnglish: Think of building a robot gym with automated staff: a Setup Manager gets the gym equipment ready, a Coach writes custom workout routines, a Trainer tests athletes on the treadmill, an Analyst reviews race footage to find flaws, and a Supervisor decides when the athlete is ready for the Olympics.
objectives: Master the 4 core RL concepts for agentic design: Policy, Reward Function, Rollout Visualization, and Iteration
Explain how the Eureka architecture is adapted into Google ADK agents and Brax HalfCheetah environments
Trace the end-to-end execution flow from root SequentialAgent entry point to RewardEvolutionLoop
Examine the 4 top-level directories: configs/, eureka_loop/, agents/, and tools/
Inspect execution logs to analyze state transitions and candidate leaderboard progressions

sections.title: Adapting Eureka for Practical Agentic Exploration
sections.content: NVIDIA's Eureka maximizes performance on high-end hardware with Isaac Gym. For our instructional masterclass, we adapt the core principles into an accessible, modular stack using: Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) for multi-agent orchestration, lightweight Brax physics environments (HalfCheetah), and Colab T4 GPU execution.

subsections.title: Core Reinforcement Learning Vocabulary
subsections.content:
• Policy: The decision-making component of the RL agent that selects joint actions given observations.
• Reward Function: The mathematical scoring rule assigning numbers to actions at each step.
• Rollout: A recorded execution of a policy in the environment rendered as an interactive 3D HTML animation.
• Iteration: One complete pass through generation, training, evaluation, reflection, and state updates.

sections.title: The 5-Step Agentic Reward Loop
sections.content: In traditional RL, reward tuning happens outside the system via manual human hacking. Eureka brings reward design inside the system as an autonomous closed loop:

subsections.title: The Execution Pipeline
subsections.content:
1. Propose: RewardDesigner writes K candidate reward functions as executable Python code.
2. Train & Evaluate: CandidateEvaluator compiles code, trains PPO policies, and records metrics & rollouts.
3. Select: SelectorAgent compares candidates and crowns the highest-fitness reward.
4. Reflect: RewardReflector analyzes training dynamics and generates structured improvement guidance.
5. Loop Control: ExitChecker assesses stopping criteria (performance thresholds or iteration limits).

sections.title: ADK Project Structure & Architectural Separation
sections.content: The codebase is organized into four distinct modular domains under `eureka_loop/`:

subsections.title: File Hierarchy
subsections.content:
• agent.py: Top-level ADK entry point assembling the pipeline via SequentialAgent.
• agents/: Decision-making units (SetupAgent, RewardDesignerOpenAIAgent, CandidateEvaluatorAgent, SelectorAgent, RewardReflector, ExitCheckerAgent).
• tools/: Execution utilities (rl_runner.py, reward_sandbox.py, scoring.py, brax_env.py, artifacts.py).
• configs/: YAML files controlling loop behavior (loop_config.yaml) and evaluation specs (task_spec_halfcheetah.yaml).

subsections.title: Sequential Orchestration Pattern
subsections.content:
root_agent = SequentialAgent(
    name='EurekaRewardEvolutionPipeline',
    sub_agents=[SetupAgent(name='SetupAgent'), build_reward_loop()]
)
This cleanly separates one-time environment grounding from iterative learning.

quiz.question: Why is visual rollout inspection essential alongside numerical fitness scores in evaluating reinforcement learning policies?
options: Because Python cannot compute numerical scores without an HTML viewer
Because agents can achieve high numerical returns by exploiting physical loopholes or moving awkwardly in unintended directions
Because rollouts are required to compile JAX kernels
Because the Google ADK framework only accepts video files as state
quiz.correctAnswer: Because agents can achieve high numerical returns by exploiting physical loopholes or moving awkwardly in unintended directions
quiz.explanation: Scalar reward returns can be deceptive. A policy might accumulate points by violently convulsing or flipping backwards. Rollout animations allow developers and reflector agents to observe the true physical behavior.

recap: The Eureka pipeline is adapted using Google ADK, Brax HalfCheetah, and Colab GPU execution.
The architecture enforces a strict boundary: agents make decisions, tools handle execution.
A SequentialAgent orchestrator runs SetupAgent once, then hands control to RewardEvolutionLoop.
Interactive 3D rollouts reveal physical loopholes that scalar return values conceal.
lessons.nextUp: SetupAgent & Environment Grounding: Loading configurations, extracting raw code, and establishing session state.

lessons.title: SetupAgent & Environment Grounding
lessons.hook: Before an AI agent can write reward functions, it needs unambiguous ground truth: What joints exist? What are the simulation bounds? Where should artifacts be stored? How does the SetupAgent establish a stable foundation for the entire pipeline?
lessons.bigIdea: The SetupAgent executes exactly once to ground the pipeline in reality: it safely parses and validates YAML configuration contracts, creates run and leaderboard directories, instantiates the Brax environment, extracts its raw Python source code as sensory context, generates a zero-shot baseline rollout, and writes all metadata into shared session state for downstream agents.
lessons.plainEnglish: Before a surgeon operates, the surgical tech prepares the sterile room, checks every instrument against a checklist, takes baseline vital signs, and puts the patient's chart on the wall. The SetupAgent does the same for our AI agents.
objectives: Implement BaseAgent subclassing and InvocationContext shared session state management in Google ADK
Enforce fail-fast configuration contracts across loop_config.yaml and task_spec.yaml
Ensure pipeline idempotency with the _setup_done guard to support workflow re-entry
Extract raw Brax environment source code to ground downstream LLM reward generation in physical reality
Generate and persist baseline rollouts and leaderboard artifacts

sections.title: Imports & Configuration Contracts
sections.content: The SetupAgent imports BaseAgent, InvocationContext, and Event from google.adk. It enforces a strict separation: the agent orchestrates lifecycle events, while tools (get_env_and_source, init_run_dir, init_leaderboard) perform file I/O and physics instantiation.

subsections.title: Enforcing the Config Contract
subsections.content: The agent validates essential keys before execution begins: env_name, iterations (int >= 1), candidates_per_iteration (int >= 1), train_steps (int >= 1), seed, and evaluation horizon/episodes. Failing fast at setup prevents costly pipeline crashes hours into training.

subsections.title: Idempotency Guard
subsections.content: By checking `ctx.session.state.get('_setup_done', False)`, the SetupAgent guarantees that resuming or re-entering an ADK workflow will never re-initialize directories or overwrite existing leaderboard artifacts.

sections.title: Extracting Environment Source Code
sections.content: The core grounding step occurs when `get_env_and_source(loop_cfg['env_name'])` is invoked. This instantiates the Brax environment and reads its underlying Python file into raw string format (`env_source`).

subsections.title: Why Extract Source Code During Setup?
subsections.content: The environment object is needed by evaluators and rollout visualizers, while the raw source code text is stored in shared state. Downstream LLMs read this exact source code to ground reward generation in the robot's actual joint degrees of freedom, mass, and velocity sensors.

sections.title: Baseline Rollout & Shared State Handoff
sections.content: Before any reward evolution takes place, the SetupAgent executes a policy rollout with random/zero actions to generate `baseline_rollout.html`. This serves as an un-trained reference point.

subsections.title: Shared State Populated
subsections.content:
ctx.session.state.update({
  '_setup_done': True,
  'loop_cfg': loop_cfg,
  'task_spec': task_spec,
  'env': env,
  'env_source': env_source,
  'outdir': str(outdir),
  'leaderboard_path': str(leaderboard_path),
  'iteration': 0
})
The agent yields an empty Event to ADK and gracefully exits, handing control to the loop.

quiz.question: What is the primary architectural purpose of the _setup_done check at the start of SetupAgent._run_async_impl()?
options: To trigger an automatic restart of the Colab notebook
To ensure workflow idempotency so resuming an interrupted run does not overwrite artifacts or reset iteration counters
To convert Brax environments into OpenAI Gym format
To clear GPU VRAM before model weights are downloaded
quiz.correctAnswer: To ensure workflow idempotency so resuming an interrupted run does not overwrite artifacts or reset iteration counters
quiz.explanation: In production agent pipelines, workflows must be idempotent. If an execution is paused or resumed, the SetupAgent recognizes that state is already established and yields immediately without overwriting run directories.

recap: SetupAgent runs once to ground the entire reward evolution pipeline.
It validates configuration contracts fail-fast before spinning up GPU training.
It extracts raw Brax Python source code and stores it in session state for LLM perception.
It generates a baseline rollout artifact to benchmark subsequent policy improvements.
lessons.nextUp: Reward Generation & Evaluator Loop: Building the RewardDesigner and CandidateEvaluator agents.

lessons.title: Reward Generation & Evaluation Loop
lessons.hook: How do you safely turn unconstrained LLM text output into executable Python math, train neural network policies with PPO without memory leaks, render interactive 3D visualizations, and handle compilation errors gracefully without crashing the pipeline?
lessons.bigIdea: The learning engine of the pipeline couples two specialized agents: RewardDesignerOpenAIAgent (which branches between zero-shot exploration and feedback-driven mutation using strict delimiter formatting and tenacity retries) and CandidateEvaluatorAgent (which sandboxes candidate code compilation, isolates JAX caches, trains PPO policies via Brax, scores fitness, persists artifacts, and serializes results into JSON state).
lessons.plainEnglish: One agent acts as the programmer writing code with strict formatting rules; the second agent acts as the quality assurance lab—it runs the code in a sandbox, trains the robot in a high-speed physics engine, catches crashes safely, records the replay video, and logs the score on the leaderboard.
objectives: Implement the RewardDesigner prompt builder supporting both Mode 1 (Exploration) and Mode 2 (Query with Feedback)
Enforce strict delimiter parsing contracts (### CANDIDATE ###) and output validation
Implement robust API call handling with tenacity exponential backoff retries
Build the CandidateEvaluator safety sandbox to compile, validate, and train generated reward code
Prevent JAX memory leaks, persist policy parameters & HTML rollouts, and serialize results for downstream reflection

sections.title: RewardDesigner: Prompt Engineering & Modes
sections.content: The RewardDesigner agent builds prompts conditioned on session state. It operates in two distinct modes:

subsections.title: Mode 1: Iteration 1 Exploration
subsections.content: When no prior best reward exists, the prompt instructs the model to generate K diverse reward candidates balancing forward velocity, stability, and control smoothness.

subsections.title: Mode 2: Iteration 2+ Mutation with Feedback
subsections.content: When a best reward exists, the prompt embeds the candidate results JSON and the reflector's textual analysis under a 'QUERY WITH FEEDBACK' block, instructing the model to generate progressive improvements of the parent reward.

subsections.title: Strict Formatting Contract
subsections.content: The system prompt enforces: plain Python only (no markdown, no backticks), def compute_reward(env_state) signature, delimiter '### CANDIDATE ###', only jnp/jax/math imports, and return total_reward, reward_terms.

sections.title: CandidateEvaluator: Sandboxed RL Execution
sections.content: The CandidateEvaluator takes raw candidate text, parses it, and executes PPO policy training under strict safety guardrails:

subsections.title: Robust Candidate Parsing
subsections.content: Removes markdown code blocks (```python), strips stray backticks, splits by delimiter line, and uses regex to extract valid `def compute_reward` blocks up to count K.

subsections.title: Sandbox Compilation & Memory Management
subsections.content: Runs `compile_reward(code)` in an isolated scope. Clears JAX backend caches (`jax.clear_caches()`) prior to training to prevent memory accumulation across candidates.

subsections.title: Training & Rollout Persistence
subsections.content: Calls `train_policy()` and `evaluate_policy()` using deterministic `seed + i`. Renders interactive `rollout.html`, saves `train_metrics.json`, `eval_metrics.json`, `policy_params.pkl`, and appends results to the CSV leaderboard.

sections.title: Graceful Fault Isolation & JSON Serialization
sections.content: If a candidate fails to compile or diverges during training, the evaluator catches the exception, writes `error.txt` into the candidate directory, logs common debugging tips, and proceeds to the next candidate without stopping the iteration.

subsections.title: JSON Serialization Contract
subsections.content: Because evaluation metrics often contain JAX arrays, the evaluator runs `convert_to_json_serializable()` before writing `ctx.session.state['candidate_results']`. Downstream agents (Selector and Reflector) read this structured JSON directly without re-scanning disk files.

quiz.question: What happens in the CandidateEvaluatorAgent if candidate 2 of 4 contains a Python syntax error or invalid JAX syntax?
options: The entire ADK pipeline crashes and terminates execution immediately
The evaluator catches the exception, saves error.txt in candidate 2's folder, logs the error, and continues evaluating candidates 3 and 4
The evaluator retries candidate 2 indefinitely until it passes
The evaluator deletes all previous candidate metrics
quiz.correctAnswer: The evaluator catches the exception, saves error.txt in candidate 2's folder, logs the error, and continues evaluating candidates 3 and 4
quiz.explanation: Production agent architectures practice fault isolation. A flawed candidate writes an error diagnostic to disk and logs the failure to the leaderboard, but the loop continues training the remaining candidates uninterrupted.

recap: RewardDesigner uses two prompt modes: broad exploration (Iter 1) and feedback mutation (Iter 2+).
Strict parsing contracts and tenacity retries ensure machine-parseable code generation.
CandidateEvaluator sandboxes compilation, isolates JAX memory, and trains PPO policies deterministically.
Per-candidate error handling guarantees that flawed LLM code never crashes the overall agentic pipeline.
lessons.nextUp: Selection, Reflection, and Human Feedback: Implementing SelectorAgent, RewardReflectorOpenAIAgent, and Human-in-the-Loop gates.

lessons.title: Selection, Reflection, and Human Feedback
lessons.hook: After the system evaluates K reward candidates, it has multiple trained policies, quantitative metrics, and rollout visualizations in state. Which candidate should carry forward, why did it succeed, and how can human insight steer the next generation?
lessons.bigIdea: The decision-making and refinement layer of the Eureka loop is handled by four specialized ADK agents: SelectorAgent deterministically picks the highest-scoring candidate without heuristics; RewardReflectorOpenAIAgent contrasts all candidate outcomes to produce diagnostic feedback; HumanReflectionAgent provides an optional 30-second terminal feedback window; and ExitCheckerAgent monitors return thresholds and patience counters to stop the loop early via ADK ToolContext escalation.
lessons.plainEnglish: Imagine an Olympic gymnastics trials: the Scorekeeper identifies the top gymnast by raw points, the Head Coach watches video of all routines to explain why the winner was cleaner, a Guest Judge can add brief notes if present, and the Committee Chair checks if the qualification score was comfortably met to end trials early.
objectives: Implement SelectorAgent to deterministically extract the best candidate from candidate_results JSON without LLM bias
Implement RewardReflectorOpenAIAgent with low-temperature comparative reasoning across both winning and failing candidates
Build HumanReflectionAgent with non-interactive TTY fallbacks and async 30-second timeout loops
Design ExitCheckerAgent with plateau patience counters and ToolContext.actions.escalate termination signals
Implement IncrementIterationAgent to advance the loop counter while pruning transient evidence and preserving long-term memory

sections.title: SelectorAgent: Deterministic Evidence-Based Selection
sections.content: Reward selection lives in `agents/selector_agent.py`. The SelectorAgent neither generates rewards nor trains policies. Its sole mandate is to read evaluation results, apply a deterministic selection rule, and update shared state.

subsections.title: Selection Implementation
subsections.content:
```python
candidate_results_json = ctx.session.state['candidate_results']
candidate_results = json.loads(candidate_results_json)
best = max(candidate_results, key=lambda x: x['score'])

ctx.session.state['best_reward_code'] = best['reward_code']
ctx.session.state['best_score'] = best['score']
ctx.session.state['best_candidate_id'] = best['candidate']
logger.info(f'[SelectorAgent] Selected candidate {best["candidate"]} with score={best["score"]:.4f}')
yield Event(author=self.name, content=None)
```

subsections.title: Design Rationale
subsections.content: Selection is purely evidence-based without LLM involvement or subjective weighting. The selector trusts the evaluator's scoring function, ensuring reproducibility and zero token overhead.

sections.title: RewardReflectorOpenAIAgent: Global Comparative Reflection
sections.content: Implemented in `agents/llm_agents.py`, this agent bridges the gap between raw scalar metrics and actionable code improvements for the next iteration.

subsections.title: Global Rather Than Local Context
subsections.content: Notice that the reflector consumes ALL candidate results, not just the winner. Comparing the best reward against failed or weaker candidates reveals critical trade-offs between velocity, joint jerk, and stability that local inspection would miss.

subsections.title: Conservative Prompting Contract
subsections.content: The agent calls the OpenAI client at temperature 0.2 with a system prompt biased toward forensic analysis rather than creativity: 'Identify why the best reward performed well, identify weaknesses, compare with failed candidates, suggest concrete reward shaping improvements, and focus on reward shaping, not policy architecture.'

sections.title: Human-in-the-Loop & Early Exit Controls
sections.content: Two critical production components make the iterative loop practical in real-world runs:

subsections.title: HumanReflectionAgent with Async Timeout
subsections.content: Runs immediately after LLM reflection. If `sys.stdin.isatty()` is false (e.g. headless CI or automated Colab), it gracefully logs and skips. If interactive, it uses `asyncio.wait_for(loop.run_in_executor(None, read_user_input), timeout=30.0)` so runs never hang if the engineer steps away.

subsections.title: ExitCheckerAgent & Plateau Patience
subsections.content: Tracks improvement against `plateau_delta`. If improvement stalls, `plateau_count` increments. Three stopping criteria: (1) Target threshold met and plateaued, (2) Performance significantly exceeds target (>= 1.1x threshold), or (3) Positive performance plateaued. It stops the loop by calling `exit_loop(tc)` which sets `tc.actions.escalate = True`.

subsections.title: IncrementIterationAgent State Pruning
subsections.content: Advances `iteration = iteration + 1` while pruning transient keys (`reward_candidates_text`, `candidate_results`, `llm_output_error`). It strictly preserves `best_reward_code`, `best_score`, `reflection`, and environment configs to prevent stale candidate leakage into future generations.

quiz.question: Why does IncrementIterationAgent explicitly delete 'candidate_results' from ctx.session.state before the next iteration begins?
options: To save memory on the hard drive
To prevent the SelectorAgent or ReflectorAgent in subsequent iterations from accidentally reusing stale scores from the previous generation
Because ADK sessions cannot hold more than 3 keys simultaneously
To force JAX to recompile the neural network weights
quiz.correctAnswer: To prevent the SelectorAgent or ReflectorAgent in subsequent iterations from accidentally reusing stale scores from the previous generation
quiz.explanation: If transient candidate evidence is not pruned, downstream agents could evaluate outdated scores if code generation encounters a partial failure, causing silent data corruption across generations.

recap: SelectorAgent makes lightweight, deterministic, evidence-based choices without LLM overhead.
RewardReflectorOpenAIAgent analyzes the full landscape of candidates at temperature 0.2 to deduce trade-offs.
HumanReflectionAgent provides an interactive 30s feedback window with resilient headless fallbacks.
ExitCheckerAgent monitors plateau counters and triggers ADK ToolContext escalation.
IncrementIterationAgent prunes transient evidence while preserving evolutionary memory.
lessons.nextUp: Loop Control, Exit Conditions, and System Behavior: Assembling agent.py and reward_loop.py into an executable end-to-end pipeline.

lessons.title: Loop Control, Exit Conditions, and System Behavior
lessons.hook: We have implemented individual agents for setup, design, evaluation, selection, reflection, human feedback, and state incrementing. How do these pieces connect into a unified, executable ADK workflow, and how do we monitor its training trajectory across iterations?
lessons.bigIdea: System orchestration in Google ADK is defined across two key assembly points: `agent.py` provides the root SequentialAgent pipeline that executes SetupAgent once before handing off to `reward_loop.py`. Inside `reward_loop.py`, a LoopAgent orchestrates the 7-agent cycle with dual termination boundaries: a configurable hard cap (`max_iterations`) and adaptive early-exit criteria via agent escalation.
lessons.plainEnglish: Think of launching a rocket: Stage 1 fires once to reach orbit (SetupAgent). Once in orbit, Stage 2 enters an automated orbital patrol loop that checks systems, performs scientific tasks, and burns thrusters until either the mission objective is verified complete or the fuel timer expires.
objectives: Construct root_agent using SequentialAgent to orchestrate SetupAgent and build_reward_loop()
Assemble the 7 sub-agents inside LoopAgent in strict execution order
Configure loop parameters and LLM model selection via loop_config.yaml
Understand dual termination: max_iterations hard cap vs ExitCheckerAgent dynamic escalation
Interpret output artifacts: timestamped run directories, iteration folders, leaderboard.csv, and rollout HTML animations

sections.title: The Two Assembly Points: agent.py & reward_loop.py
sections.content: ADK pipelines maintain clean separation between the top-level discovery entry point and nested loop construction:

subsections.title: Entrypoint: agent.py
subsections.content:
```python
from google.adk.agents import SequentialAgent
from .agents.setup_agent import SetupAgent
from .agents.reward_loop import build_reward_loop

root_agent = SequentialAgent(
    name='EurekaRewardEvolutionPipeline',
    sub_agents=[
        SetupAgent(name='SetupAgent'),
        build_reward_loop(),
    ],
    description='Initializes env/task state and runs a Eureka-like reward evolution loop.'
)
```

subsections.title: Loop Factory: reward_loop.py
subsections.content:
```python
def build_reward_loop():
    loop_cfg = _load_yaml('configs/loop_config.yaml')
    model = loop_cfg.get('openai_model', 'gpt-4o-mini')
    return LoopAgent(
        name='RewardEvolutionLoop',
        sub_agents=[
            RewardDesignerOpenAIAgent(model=model),
            CandidateEvaluatorAgent(),
            SelectorAgent(name='SelectorAgent'),
            RewardReflectorOpenAIAgent(model=model),
            HumanReflectionAgent(name='HumanReflectionAgent'),
            ExitCheckerAgent(name='ExitCheckerAgent'),
            IncrementIterationAgent(name='IncrementIterationAgent'),
        ],
        max_iterations=loop_cfg['iterations']
    )
```

sections.title: Execution Modes & Artifact Flight Recorder
sections.content: Because PPO training across multiple candidates is compute-intensive, we support two modes: live Google Colab execution on T4 GPUs, or inspecting pre-run notebooks and rollout artifacts.

subsections.title: Run Directory Structure
subsections.content:
Each run creates a timestamped folder containing:
• `iteration_001/`, `iteration_002/`: Per-iteration candidate folders with `reward.py`, `train_metrics.json`, and `rollout.html`.
• `leaderboard.csv`: Persistent log tracking all candidates, returns, and scores.
• `rollout_baseline.html`: Initial policy benchmark prior to reward learning.
• `loop_config.json`, `task_spec.json`, and `env_code.py`: Complete environmental audit trail.

subsections.title: Interpreting Rollouts vs Scores
subsections.content: Leaderboard scores show which candidate accumulated the most points. However, 3D HTML rollouts reveal physical reality: Did the cheetah actually sprint forward, or did it exploit physics to flip backwards or twitch at high speed? Rollouts catch reward hacking early.

quiz.question: In the ADK reward loop, how is early termination communicated from the ExitCheckerAgent to the enclosing LoopAgent?
options: By throwing a Python RuntimeError exception
By setting tool_context.actions.escalate = True inside exit_loop, signaling the LoopAgent to break its iteration cycle
By deleting the configs/loop_config.yaml file from disk
By overwriting the iteration counter with infinity
quiz.correctAnswer: By setting tool_context.actions.escalate = True inside exit_loop, signaling the LoopAgent to break its iteration cycle
quiz.explanation: Google ADK uses structured event actions. Setting `actions.escalate = True` via a tool context cleanly informs parent orchestrators (like LoopAgent) to terminate without crashing the process.

recap: `agent.py` uses SequentialAgent to cleanly separate one-time setup from the iterative loop.
`reward_loop.py` configures the 7-agent cycle with dual termination (hard cap + dynamic exit).
The system persists an audit trail: iteration folders, leaderboard.csv, and interactive rollouts.
Rollout visualizations detect reward hacking behaviors that scalar returns fail to reveal.
lessons.nextUp: Thinking Through Eureka: Design a Smart Parking Multi-Agent System (Interactive Architectural Challenge).

lessons.title: Thinking Through Eureka: Smart Parking Agent System
lessons.hook: We've mastered autonomous reward learning in robotics simulation. Now, how do we apply agentic design principles to transform a traditional, reactive microservices architecture into a proactive, resilient multi-agent system?
lessons.bigIdea: In this architectural thought exercise, we evolve a traditional smart parking service (SensorService, BookingService, UserService, NotificationService) into a proactive multi-agent system. By designing DriverAgent, ZoneAgent, and ReservationAgent with 4-part internal architectures, choosing hybrid orchestration patterns, and implementing rigorous safety guardrails, we demonstrate how agentic principles scale to real-world autonomous operations.
lessons.plainEnglish: A traditional parking app is like a vending machine: you press a button, and if a spot is open, it spits out a ticket. An agentic parking system is like a team of valet concierges: one greets the driver and knows their habits, one monitors the garage zones and weather, and one coordinates payments and locks spots without double-booking.
objectives: Contrast reactive microservices against proactive agentic architectures across reasoning, personalization, and error recovery
Evaluate Centralized (Manager-Worker) vs Decentralized orchestration trade-offs in scalability and fault tolerance
Design 4-part internal agent architectures (Input Interface, Reasoning Core, Tools, Memory) for DriverAgent, ZoneAgent, and ReservationAgent
Select tailored internal orchestration patterns: ReAct for drivers, Plan-and-Execute for zones, and State Machines for reservations
Implement robust safety guardrails addressing double-booking, financial limits, and location privacy

sections.title: The Need for Agency: Beyond Reactive Microservices
sections.content: Traditional microservices wait for central application logic to call them. They struggle with proactive assistance (rerouting before traffic jams), complex multi-factor reasoning (dynamic pricing based on concerts and weather), personalized recommendations (remembering EV charger preferences), and robust sensor error handling.

subsections.title: The Agentic Insight
subsections.content: Agentic architecture is the right choice when a system must move beyond fixed rules into goal-oriented, autonomous reasoning under uncertainty.

sections.title: Hybrid Orchestration & 4-Part Agent Architectures
sections.content: We adopt a hybrid orchestration model: a centralized Coordinator/Manager balances global zone demand while specialized agents operate with defined internal architectures:

subsections.title: DriverAgent
subsections.content:
• Input: Natural language chat, GPS telemetry, calendar events.
• Reasoning: ReAct conversational loop balancing price, walking distance, and EV charging needs.
• Tools: Maps API, UserProfile API, Reservation request API.
• Memory: Short-term trip context + long-term vehicle specs and spot preferences.

subsections.title: ZoneAgent
subsections.content:
• Input: Manager capacity queries, sensor telemetry streams, local event alerts.
• Reasoning: Multi-step Plan-and-Execute analyzing sensor confidence, traffic surges, and dynamic surge pricing.
• Tools: SensorService API, EventRegistry API, ZoneTariff tool.
• Memory: Historical hourly occupancy curves and hardware sensor fault logs.

subsections.title: ReservationAgent
subsections.content:
• Input: Reservation intent with zone and spot specifications.
• Reasoning: Strict transactional state machine (Hold -> Authorize -> Confirm -> Notify).
• Tools: BookingService API, PaymentGateway API, NotificationService API.
• Memory: Transaction idempotency keys and active hold lease timers.

sections.title: Safety Guardrails: Concurrency, Finance, & Privacy
sections.content: Autonomous agents require rigorous guardrails to prevent real-world harm:

subsections.title: Double-Booking Prevention
subsections.content: Enforces 2-minute distributed locks (Redis lease) via ReservationAgent so multiple DriverAgents cannot confirm the same physical bay simultaneously.

subsections.title: Financial Transaction Bounds
subsections.content: ZoneAgent dynamic pricing has hard minimum ($2/hr) and maximum ($25/hr) clamp boundaries, and charges above $50 trigger mandatory Driver confirmation.

subsections.title: Privacy Isolation
subsections.content: Driver location telemetry is ephemerally processed in session memory and scrubbed before long-term storage, preventing user tracking leakage.

quiz.question: Why is a strict transactional state machine orchestration pattern preferred over open-ended ReAct loops for the ReservationAgent?
options: Because LLMs cannot read booking databases
Because booking and payment requires deterministic atomicity, two-phase commits, and automatic rollback on failure to prevent double-charging or orphaned holds
Because state machines consume fewer GPU CUDA cores
Because Google ADK only supports state machines
quiz.correctAnswer: Because booking and payment requires deterministic atomicity, two-phase commits, and automatic rollback on failure to prevent double-charging or orphaned holds
quiz.explanation: Financial transactions and spot allocations must be atomic and reversible. An open-ended ReAct loop risks unexpected tool ordering or partial execution, whereas a transactional state machine guarantees idempotency and rollback.

recap: Agentic architectures evolve reactive microservices into proactive, goal-oriented reasoning systems.
Hybrid orchestration balances centralized coordination with specialized, autonomous worker agents.
Agents are structured with 4 pillars: Input Interface, Reasoning Core, Tools, and Memory.
Different agent roles require distinct orchestration patterns (ReAct for drivers, State Machines for transactions).
Distributed locks, price clamps, and privacy scrubbing provide defense-in-depth guardrails.
lessons.nextUp: Module 11: ChainBuddy — Solving the Blank Page Problem in LLM Evaluation Pipelines.
